items.stimulus: Birdwatchers often report that blackbirds in cities sing at a higher pitch than blackbirds in forests. Many ornithologists have been skeptical, suspecting that listeners only perceive city songs as higher because traffic noise masks the lower notes. items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

D.why: You reversed the evidence. The skeptics doubted that a real pitch difference exists, and the instruments found one (3.4 vs. 2.8 kilohertz). That finding goes against their doubt, so it cannot justify it.

items.stimulus: Many astronomers had long held that the dim companion orbiting the star Tessin-4 was a brown dwarf, an object too small to shine as a true star, because its surface is unusually cool. D.why: You mixed up who did what. The astronomers assumed the companion was a brown dwarf. The result is measured evidence, and evidence doesn't assume anything. You gave the result a verb that belongs to the people who held the view.

items.stimulus: Historians of printmaking had long ______ that the uneven ink in the engravings of eighteenth-century printer Mathilde Corvage reflected careless workmanship. D.why: To anticipate something is to come before it and expect it. The view was already held for a long time before Prakash's work, and her findings oppose it rather than look ahead to it.

"Because" ties their belief to the missing markings: with nothing on the page telling them otherwise, they took for granted that the pieces should be played at one even volume. items.subtype_name: How findings relate to a claim (support / undermine / question)
items.stimulus: Some geologists have argued that the fault beneath the Arreda Valley is inactive, pointing to more than four centuries without a recorded earthquake there. Seismologist Tomás Oyelaran and colleagues placed highly sensitive instruments along the fault for two years and detected thousands of tremors too faint to be felt, clustered along its entire length. These measurements therefore ______ the claim of inactivity, indicating that the fault is still slowly slipping.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: The claim is that the fault is inactive. The team recorded thousands of tremors along it, and "indicating that the fault is still slowly slipping" spells out the conclusion: the fault is active. The blank links the measurements to the claim, so you need a verb meaning that the evidence weakens the claim. "Undermine" is that verb, and "therefore" shows it follows directly from the tremor data.

A.why: You picked a neutral verb that sounds scientific. Researchers inspect things, but measurements don't, and even if they did, "inspect" wouldn't say whether the data agree or disagree with the claim.

B.why: You reversed the relationship. Thousands of tremors show that the fault is moving, which goes against the claim that it is inactive. The final clause, "still slowly slipping," makes clear the claim is being knocked down.

C.why: The claim of inactivity was made before these measurements, and the measurements oppose it. They don't come before it or expect it, so "anticipate" gets both the timing and the direction wrong.
